summary: Formats a value as a percentage string: fetches the value through a virtual call at vtable+180, normalizes it by the range width this+0xF8 minus this+0xF4, scales by 100.0, truncates with CRTFtol, renders "%d%%" via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck, and stores the result with StringCopyWithBufferRealloc. A flag at this+0xF0 selects signed-int vs float interpretation of the fetched value. Returns 0.

local_names.v3: pointer to the value returned by the virtual getter
local_names.v7: stack format buffer (61 bytes + trailing v8/v9)

operations.description: Initialize the local format buffer: copy the first byte of byte_5EA438 into v7[0], zero-fill the remaining 60 bytes, and zero the trailing v8/v9 words.
Virtual method dispatch: read the vtable pointer at this+0x0 and call the method at vtable slot +180 on this, receiving a pointer to the value to be formatted.
Signedness branch on the flag at this+0xF0: when set, read the value as a signed int; otherwise read it as a float.
Normalize the fetched value by dividing it by the range width (this+0xF8 minus this+0xF4, i.e. this[62]-this[61]).
Scale the normalized value by 100.0 and truncate to an integer with CRTFtol; the 100.0 percent-scale constant is conventionally attributed to the float constant flt_59E6F8.
Format the integer as a percentage into the local buffer with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck using the "%d%%" format string (global aD).
Copy/stash the formatted string via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc.
